title: Settings
summary: The user's OpenRouter API key, and the model the agent runs on.
description: The agent has a section of its own in the app's settings, named after its profession.

requirements.text: The user enters an OpenRouter API key in the agent's settings.
A key is checked with OpenRouter when it is saved, and the settings say whether it was accepted and, if not, why.
The key is kept in the operating system's store for secrets, never in the app's database, so it is never synced, exported or backed up with the data.

deprecation.reason: Out of scope for this part: where the product keeps secrets is the product's own decision, not the agent's.

requirements.text: A saved key is shown only by its last four characters, and can be replaced or removed.
The settings list the models OpenRouter offers that can call tools, fetched when the settings open, and the user picks one.
Each model in the list shows its name, its provider, how much context it takes and its price per million input and output tokens.
The list of models can be searched by name and provider.
When OpenRouter no longer offers the chosen model, the settings and the chat say so, and the chat asks for another before it sends.
When the list of models can't be fetched, the settings say why and keep the chosen model.
The settings say that what the agent reads from the app is sent to OpenRouter and to the provider of the chosen model.
The settings show the credit left on the key.
